cards.front: Who supplies most of a PE fund's capital, and what is their liability?
cards.back: LPs supply almost all capital; liability is limited to their committed amount.

cards.front: What does the GP do, and how is it paid?
cards.back: Manages the fund (sourcing, deals, exits); paid a management fee plus carried interest, and invests a GP commitment.

cards.front: What is the difference between committed and paid-in capital?
cards.back: Committed is what the LP agreed to provide; paid-in is what has actually been called and funded.

cards.front: What is the J-curve and why does it happen?
cards.back: The early dip in net returns from fees and early markdowns before exits; returns climb later as winners are realized.

cards.front: What does "2 and 20" mean?
cards.back: 2% annual management fee, 20% carried interest. Both are negotiable defaults, not laws.

cards.front: Committed-capital vs invested-capital fee base: which favors whom?
cards.back: Committed favors the GP (paid on undrawn capital); invested favors LPs (paid only on deployed capital).

cards.front: Describe a typical fee step-down.
cards.back: Fee on committed capital during the investment period, then a lower rate and/or a switch to invested cost in the harvest years.

cards.front: Roughly what share of committed capital do lifetime fees consume, per Metrick & Yasuda?
cards.back: Median ~12% for buyout and ~17.75% for VC funds (1993-2006 sample). A flat 2% for 10 yrs would be 20%.

cards.front: Per Metrick & Yasuda, what share of expected GP revenue is fixed (fee-like) vs performance-based?
cards.back: About two-thirds is fixed (fees), undercutting the "only paid if they perform" narrative.

cards.front: What is a management-fee offset and what is the current standard?
cards.back: Portfolio-company fees reduce the management fee LPs owe; 100% (dollar-for-dollar) offset is now standard, and ILPA recommends it.

cards.front: Name three fees a GP may charge portfolio companies.
cards.back: Transaction/deal fees, monitoring fees, director/board fees (also advisory/consulting).

cards.front: What is recycling and what does ILPA say about it?
cards.back: Reinvesting early proceeds to offset fee drag; ILPA: capped or monitored, investment-period only.

cards.front: What is carried interest and the standard rate?
cards.back: The GP's share of profits; standard 20%.

cards.front: Gross vs net carry, and ILPA's view?
cards.back: Gross = on profit before fees/expenses; net = after. ILPA requires net.

cards.front: How much extra is an investment-capital carry basis worth to a GP vs committed-capital, approximately?
cards.back: Per M&Y, roughly the carry rate times lifetime fees (ignoring discounting), for a profitable fund.

cards.front: What is a preferred return / hurdle and the standard level?
cards.back: Minimum LP return before GP carry; ~8% compounded in PE (6-7% private credit; often none in VC).

cards.front: Hard hurdle vs soft hurdle?
cards.back: Hard: carry only on profit above the hurdle (no catch-up). Soft: hurdle plus catch-up, so GP eventually earns full carry % on all profit.

cards.front: Which does ILPA prefer and what does it concede?
cards.back: The hard hurdle; ILPA concedes it means the GP will not actually receive the full stated carry percentage.

cards.front: Name three ways a GP can make a high headline hurdle less LP-friendly.
cards.back: Use gross IRR, simple (not compounded) accrual, full catch-up, or delay the pref start date to after the investment period.

cards.front: What does a 100% GP catch-up achieve at high returns?
cards.back: It restores the GP to its full carry % of all profit, including the pref portion; the hurdle becomes a timing gate only.

cards.front: For a 20% carry and 100% catch-up, what is the catch-up dollar amount relative to the pref paid?
cards.back: 0.25 × pref (since C = c/(1−c) × pref = 0.20/0.80 × pref).

cards.front: On $100M, 5-yr, 8% pref, where do the two carry kink points fall (Example 1)?
cards.back: Kink 1 at $46,932,807.68 profit (pref paid, carry begins); Kink 2 at $58,666,009.60 (catch-up complete, GP at 20% of all profit).

cards.front: List the four European waterfall tiers in order.
cards.back: Return of capital, preferred return, GP catch-up, 80/20 split.

cards.front: European vs American in one sentence each.
cards.back: European: no carry until all fund capital + whole-fund pref returned. American: carry per realized deal once that deal clears its own hurdle.

cards.front: Which is more LP-friendly and why?
cards.back: European; winners cannot pay GP carry while losers are unrealized, so the GP never earns carry while the fund is underwater.

cards.front: In Example 1 ($100M→$200M), what does the GP receive and what % of profit is it?
cards.back: $20,000,000, exactly 20% of the $100,000,000 profit (full catch-up).

cards.front: Same inputs but a hard hurdle (no catch-up): GP carry?
cards.back: $10,613,438.46, about 10.6% of profit, roughly half.

cards.front: What is a clawback and why does deal-by-deal need it?
cards.back: GP returns excess carry at wind-up; deal-by-deal can overpay the GP on early winners before later losers realize.

cards.front: In Example 2, how much clawback and why?
cards.back: $6,000,000: GP banked $20M on Deal A, but 20% of true $70M fund profit is $14M.

cards.front: Post-clawback, how do American and European economics compare in Example 2?
cards.back: Identical end split (GP $14M / LP $156M); they differ only in timing and clawback (counterparty) risk.

cards.front: What is ILPA's clawback tax stance in 3.0?
cards.back: Compute clawback gross of taxes; reverts to the 2009 position, disliked by GPs.

cards.front: What is ILPA and is it a regulator?
cards.back: The Institutional Limited Partners Association, an LP best-practice body; not a regulator.

cards.front: Define DPI, RVPI, TVPI.
cards.back: DPI = distributions/paid-in (realized); RVPI = NAV/paid-in (unrealized); TVPI = DPI + RVPI (total multiple).

cards.front: What does a KS-PME above 1.0 mean, and how does Direct Alpha relate to it?
cards.back: KS-PME > 1 means PE beat the public index; Direct Alpha is the annualized version of KS-PME (the IRR of index-compounded cash flows).
